issues.failure_explanation: When \(\tau=0\), the strict stopping test can never hold. Once the residual is zero—including for an exact initial guess—the algorithm proceeds with \(\vec p^k=0\) and computes \(\alpha_k=0/0\), so it is not well defined on its stated input class.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require \(\tau>0\), or use a non-strict stopping test that terminates when the residual is zero before forming the quotients.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm and the convergence theorem do not cover all tolerances and initial guesses claimed in their statements.
issues.title: CG breaks down for the allowed zero tolerance

The approximation property imposed later would exclude this example, but it is not an input condition of the algorithm itself.

issues.failure_explanation: If \(\rho_{\ell'}=0\) on an intermediate level, or \(\rho_\ell=0\) on the finest level, both numerator and denominator of the corresponding step size are zero. This occurs in particular for the exact input \(u_\ell=u_\ell^\star\), for which every residual and correction vanishes. Thus \(\Phi_\ell\) is undefined on an input explicitly included in the contraction claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that a zero level correction is skipped and assign any harmless step size there, so that the resulting contribution remains zero.
issues.overall_effect: The multigrid update, its matrix representation, and the induced GPCG guarantee are not literally defined for all claimed inputs, including the zero residual required by the all-vector preconditioner assumption.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition \(\ref{lemma: MG contraction}\) concerns Algorithm \(\ref{algo: geometric MG}\) with its residual-dependent intermediate step sizes and its optimal finest-level step size. The paper then replaces all positive-level step sizes by a fixed value and merely asserts that all results remain valid. The corollary's proof critically uses the resulting unproved uniform bound \(\|E_\ell\|_{A_\ell}\le q<1\) to establish both positive definiteness and the condition-number estimate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a contraction proof for the fixed-step one-sided multigrid error propagator, with an \(h\)- and \(p\)-independent factor below one; the symmetric argument can then use that factor rather than the unqualified factor from the adaptive-step proposition.

issues.title: Fixed-step multigrid contraction is asserted without establishing it
issues.why_classification: The missing contraction estimate is a nontrivial multilevel argument essential to the result, but it is a contained supporting lemma and would not require changing the overall symmetric-preconditioning architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Finite patch overlap controls the sum of squared local norms, \(\sum_z\|w\|_{\omega_z}^2\), not the unsquared sum appearing here. If \(w\) has equal nonzero energy on many mutually separated patches, the displayed left side grows like the square root of the number of patches relative to \(\|w\|\). Hence the claimed mesh-independent estimate is false, and Step 2 does not prove the strengthened Cauchy--Schwarz bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Step 1–2 by a localized estimate retaining local norms of both factors, followed by Cauchy–Schwarz over the bounded-overlap patches, or supply another nontrivial proof of the stated generation-wise operator bound.
issues.overall_effect: The upper spectral bound for the additive Schwarz operator and the resulting uniform condition-number and PCG optimality claims are not established.
issues.title: Finite overlap is incorrectly used to bound a sum of local norms
issues.why_classification: The false estimate cannot be repaired by routine algebra; it needs a materially different localized argument, but the repair is confined to the strengthened Cauchy–Schwarz lemma and need not change the additive Schwarz construction.
